note: Every case of DALgo's join and subquery fixtures (dtql/testdata/joins and dtql/testdata/subqueries in the DALgo module the build uses, read from the module cache and never edited) that this server answers differently from its fixture or refuses, on the engine named, with the status it gets. TestRelationalFixtureCorpusOverHTTP posts each document to a SQLite mount and to a local inGitDB mount, on /v1/databases/{id}/dtql and on /v1/dtql, and fails on a case that is neither equal to its fixture nor listed here, and on an entry that has become equal. Only the spelling of a document is rewritten by the test: the default schema of a source is dropped, and on /v1/dtql every source names its database. The join fixtures ship no dataset, so testdata/joins-chinook holds the one DALgo's own test builds in code, with empty tables for the collections of the two documents that fail to parse; the subquery fixtures run on their own dataset.json and schema.json. Every table of a SQLite mount gets an integer key column id, which an OpenVaultDB SQLite mount keys its records by. An answer is compared by its rows in order, as JSON values, and an error by the category and path of the diagnostic inside a 400 invalid_dtql, not by its wording. A relational answer is not passed through the schema coercion of the single-collection path, so a declared boolean of a SQLite mount is 0 or 1 in a relational row and true or false in a single-collection record; no fixture holds a boolean, and this applies to every case below. Companion files that are not documents (membership-null-table.expect.json, exists-short-circuit.expect.json) are not run.

divergences.reason: The database route expands the wildcard from the columns of the table, so the key column id, which the declared schema does not list, is part of every row.
The in-memory route is given no ordered field list by the mount, so the wildcard cannot be expanded and the document is refused.
The in-memory route is given no field lists by the mounts, so an unqualified name that two sources carry is bound to the first source instead of being refused as ambiguous.
